get.summary: OAuth2 authorization server metadata (RFC 8414).
List API keys for the authenticated account.
get.description:
Secrets are never returned: only the stored prefix/suffix fragments, the
key type, scopes, stored ingest settings and lifecycle timestamps. Revoked keys are
omitted; expired ones are included so the customer can see why a key
stopped working rather than watching it silently disappear.

The response stays a bare array, unchanged in shape from before hashing,
so a dashboard build that predates this deploy still renders the list.

post.summary: Create a new API key for the authenticated account.
post.description:
The response contains the full secret. This is the ONLY time it is ever
shown: only its SHA-256 is stored, so it cannot be retrieved again, only
rotated.

`key_type` defaults to `full` when omitted, which is exactly what every
key did before this endpoint grew types. The dashboard sends `ingest`
explicitly, because a key destined for a log-forwarder config should not
also be able to delete monitors.

200.description: Newly minted API key; the secret is only returned once

400.description: Invalid name, scopes, expiry or ingest settings, or key cap reached

403.description: Caller is not an admin

delete.summary: Revoke an API key.
delete.description:
The route and verb are unchanged, so the dashboard's existing delete
button keeps working, but the row is now kept and stamped `revoked_at`
instead of being deleted. Revocation takes effect immediately: both the
customer API and the ingest authorizers check `revoked_at` on every
request. Keeping the row preserves the audit history of a credential that
may have been used to change things.

Revoked keys disappear from `GET /account/api_key`, which is exactly what
a delete looked like before.

Deliberately idempotent: an unknown or already-revoked id still returns
200. The M2M equivalent 404s on an unknown id, but this endpoint has
always returned 200 for one (the DELETE simply matched no rows), and a
caller that has been relying on that must not start seeing errors.

post.summary:
Rotate an API key: mint a replacement and revoke the predecessor, in one
transaction.
post.description:
Because the secret is hashed at rest there is no "reveal it again", so
rotation is how a customer recovers from a lost or leaked key. The new key
inherits the old one's name, type, scopes, expiry and stored ingest settings.
Rotation preserves older stored values without create-time validation.

The old secret stops working the moment this returns; there is no grace
period. A caller that needs overlap should instead create a second key,
deploy it, then revoke the first.

200.description: New key; the secret is only returned once

404.description: API key not found or already revoked

post.summary: Create a managed client account under the calling partner.
post.description:
The client is a perfectly ordinary account with a parent pointer: it has
its own monitors, its own status pages, its own quotas and its own
notification routing, and the partner works in it through the
`X-SQ-Account` header. Three things make it not-ordinary, all decided here
rather than inside the shared provisioning seam:

* **No Stripe customer.** The partner is billed on one subscription; a
  client is never billed directly, so it never gets a customer object to
  leak or reconcile.
* **No welcome email.** The contact never asked us for an account. A
  "welcome to Site Qwality" email out of nowhere is the partner's
  relationship to manage, not ours.
* **A Stytch organization with no member and no session.** Nobody is
  signing in yet. The organization exists up front so the partner's later
  invite has somewhere to land, and the local user row (which the account
  needs, for `primary_user_id`) carries a NULL `stytch_member_id` until
  then.

Marks the client account deleted and nothing else. That single flag is what
every downstream consequence keys on, and each one is what removing a client
should mean:

* the client's own users lose access,
* the client's checks stop running,
* the client can no longer be opened with `X-SQ-Account`, and
* the client slot is freed immediately, so you can add a replacement.

The client's data is retained per the retention policy. **This is not an
erasure endpoint.** Suspension history is left intact.

put.description:
A partner picks a bundle, never individual packs: the wholesale rate is flat
per client, so what a client gets is one of the two compositions that rate
was priced against.

The bundle becomes ordinary subscription rows on the client account, so
quota metering, paid feature unlocks and every other downstream consequence
behave exactly as they do for a direct customer.

**Idempotent, and that is the intended way to use it.** Setting the bundle a
client is already on grants nothing, cancels nothing, and does not move a
billing anniversary, so a console that re-asserts state on every save is
safe.

Changing a client's bundle moves that client between the wholesale lines on
your own subscription, prorated for the remainder of the current period.

manual_expiry_date.description:
The renewal date the customer entered themselves.

For the TLDs in [`crate::domain_expiry::NO_EXPIRY_TLDS`], whose
registries publish no date under any protocol, this is the only date
there can be, and the normal 90/60/30/7/0 ladder runs against it.

**When a registry date also exists, the registry wins** and this stays
visible beside it rather than being discarded. A stale manual date is
exactly the silent wrongness domain monitoring exists to remove, so it
never overrides the authority; but dropping it would leave the customer
believing they had entered a date that was doing something. Seeing the
two disagree is the information. `expiry_source` says which of them
`expiry_date` currently is.

DERIVED from the domain, never stored, so it can never go stale against
the curated list. `false` for the eleven TLDs measured as publishing
nothing, and that is the flag a UI keys "offer the manual entry field"
off. It is `true` for every TLD not positively established otherwise,
including every TLD nobody has looked at, which is what makes the default
safe: being wrong in this direction costs three failed lookups, and being
wrong the other way silently removes a customer's check.

last_failure_reason.description:
Why the last check could not read the registry, if it could not.

One of `no_rdap_endpoint`, `registry_no_record`, `no_whois_server`,
`whois_no_record`, `whois_access_denied`, `rate_limited`,
`transport_error`, `malformed_response`, `no_source_has_a_record`, or
`registry_publishes_no_expiry`.

**`registry_publishes_no_expiry` is a STATE, not a failure**, and a UI
must not present it as a broken check. It means the chain was never run
because this registry publishes nothing, and the customer's next move is
to enter a date, not to open a support ticket. `registry_publishes_expiry`
above is the same fact in the form a client can branch on.

A failed check DELIBERATELY leaves `expiry_date`, `domain_status`,
`registrar` and `nameservers` untouched: it learned nothing, and clearing
them would erase a good date over a transient blip and re-arm every alert
rung. So a non-null value here means the sibling fields are LAST KNOWN
rather than current, and a UI should say so. Cleared on the next
successful check.

and it is invisible from the job row alone.

`token` query param and POSTs it to `/auth/magic-link/authenticate`.
Defaults to `${base_frontend_url}/auth/magic-link/callback`. When we
send the email instead, its path and query become the `redirect_path`,
and only on the frontend's own origin.

turnstile_response.description:
Cloudflare Turnstile token from the sign-in or sign-up widget. Required
wherever Turnstile is configured.

aggregations.description: Allowed aggregations; empty means the measure is already reduced (uptime, counts).

scalar_only.description: Only meaningful as a single value (for example open incidents now).

MemberInfo.description: Full member info returned on every authentication response.

source_ids.description: The incidents to merge into the one in the path (1 to 20).

MergedIncidentResponse.description: An incident merged into this one; its updates stay on it.

series_ids.description: Decimal UInt64 strings from the series endpoint, at most 100.

interval.description: T2 interval or auto, with at most 300 buckets per series.

aggregation.description: Last ingested sample per bucket, kind and flags, without rate or increase math.

MetricQuery.description: A metrics query (design 6.5.4): lettered queries, formulas over them, one window.

compare.description: Overlay the same query this long ago, as `1w`.

show.description: Query and formula ids to draw; empty draws the formulas, or every query when none.

oneOf.description: Absent: the T13 default for the metric's type (histograms: `merge`, `merge`).

MfaMethod.description: A second factor the member can complete MFA with.

MfaRequiredResponse.description:
Answer of any login endpoint when the member has confirmed TOTP. The
frontend checks `mfa_required` before reading an `AuthResponse`.

kind.description:
`quota_not_checked`, `schedule_missing`, `tls_unknown`, `inconclusive_run`, `degraded_quorum`,
`partial_failure`, `recovery_pending`, `recovery_reset`, `recovery_confirmed`, `flap_started`,
`flap_held`, `flap_break_through` or `flap_ended`. New kinds may be added.

MonitorTotalsByType.description:
Account-wide monitor counts split by monitor type.

All three keys are ALWAYS present, including for a type the account has
none of, which is why this is a struct and not a map. A dashboard tile
that reads a missing key renders nothing at all, and "nothing" reads as a
stuck loading state rather than as zero.

MonitorType.description:
Which table a unified monitor row came from.

The dashboard maps this straight onto the `_type` field its table and cell
renderers key off, and splits the page back into per-type slices with it.
It is the one field on the row that is never null.

MonitorTypeTotals.description:
The four monitor counts for one monitor type.

Same four numbers, same meaning, as the top level of
`AccountMonitorTotals`, restricted to a single type.

MonitorsPage.description: One server-filtered, server-sorted page of the unified monitor list.

total.description:
Number of monitors matching the filters, across every page. This is
what "X-Y of N" is built from; it is not the length of `items`.

NetworkCapture.description:
Network request capture. Method, status, timing and sizes are always recorded; headers only
when allowlisted, bodies only for matching URLs.

header_allowlist.description: Lower-case header names recorded on requests and responses.

body_urls.description:
URL prefixes (a path on the page's origin, or an http(s) URL) whose JSON or text bodies
are recorded.

trace_urls.description: URL prefixes, as `body_urls`, that receive a `traceparent` header.

resource_route.description: The request path with ids collapsed.

req_body.description: Captured bodies, redacted; needs body access.

n.description: Requests this row aggregates (repeats of one successful request within 30 s).

NotCheckedReason.description: Why an active monitor is not being checked. Serialized as `not_checked_reason`.

oneOf.description:
How this channel's recent deliveries went: whether the last alert
reached anyone, and why not when it did not (a revoked Slack token, a
bouncing inbox). Present on the read endpoints; absent on create and
update responses.

is_default.description: The group monitors get when they are created without `group_notification_ids`.

flap_hold.description: Hold alerts while a monitor flaps. Monitors follow it unless they set their own.

outage_ack_stops_repeats.description:
Acknowledging an outage stops its repeat alerts. When false, an
acknowledgement only records who is on it.

updated_at.description: When the settings were last saved; `null` while they are the defaults.

updated_by_user_id.description: Who saved them last, when a member did.

updated_by_name.description: That member's name, or their email when they have no name.

OAuthAuthorizeRequest.description: The member's decision on the consent screen.

scopes.description: The scopes the member granted: a subset of the requested ones.

redirect_uri.description:
Where to send the browser next: back to the app, with the code or the
denial attached.

OAuthAuthorizeStartRequest.description: The OAuth request the consent page received, passed through for checking.

scopes.description: The requested scopes, split from the space-separated `scope` param.

consent_required.description:
False when the member already approved this app for these scopes;
the page can then continue without asking again.

OAuthConnectCompleteRequest.description: Complete an in-session OAuth provider attach.

oauth_token.description: Token from the Stytch redirect (`?token=` on the callback URL).

OAuthConnectStartResponse.description: Start URL for attaching an OAuth provider while already signed in.

url.description: Stytch public OAuth start URL. The browser navigates here directly.

provider.description: Provider identifier. Currently "google" (Branch C will add "github").

ok.description:
Always true. Present because a successful response with an empty body
hands the dashboard's request wrapper a falsy `data`, which reads as a
failure at the call site.

OnCallLayerVersionResponse.description:
One version of a layer: an ended one, or the current one (`effective_until` absent unless the
layer itself ends).

timezone.description: Ended versions always name their zone; the current one only when it has its own.

ended_by_user_id.description: Who made the edit that ended this version.

OnCallLayerVersionsResponse.description: A layer's history: every ended version, then the current one.

OnCallNowResponse.description: Who a schedule has on call at `at`, until when, and who comes next.

oneOf.description: The shift that starts when `on_call` ends; absent when that is beyond 90 days.

OnCallReportResponse.description: Who carried the on-call load over a range, and where the schedules had gaps.

OnCallReportUser.description: One person's on-call load over the report range.

off_hours_seconds.description: Part of `on_call_seconds` outside 09:00 to 18:00, Monday to Friday, in the schedule's zone.

pages.description: Responder pages accepted for them, and the incidents those pages were for.

handoff_day.description:
Weekly layers only: weekday of the handoff, 0 = Sunday .. 6 = Saturday,
interpreted together with `handoff_time` in the schedule's timezone.

timezone.description: The layer's own IANA zone for handoffs and restrictions; absent means the schedule's.

restrictions.description: Windows the layer covers; empty means always.

oneOf.description: Where the rotation is counted from: absent on layers created before anchors were stored.

version.description: The current version's number (1 until the layer is edited). Set by the edit and versions routes.

version_started_at.description: When the current version took over. Set by the edit and versions routes.

OnCallShiftResponse.description:
A stretch of a schedule with one answer. `starts_at` or `ends_at` is absent when the stretch
runs more than 90 days past the instant or range asked about.

user_id.description: Who is on call; absent in a gap.

OnCallShiftsResponse.description: A schedule's final timeline over a range, gaps included.

OnCallSourceKind.description: Why someone is on call, or `gap` when nobody is.

OutageAcknowledgement.description: One outage's acknowledgement. The first one wins and never changes.

transition_id.description: The outage: the monitor's DOWN state transition.

acknowledged_by_user_id.description: `null` for an email link or an API key.

acknowledged_by_name.description: The member's name, or their email when they have no name.

status.description:
Stripe's own subscription status, or `null` when the account has never
subscribed. Deliberately the raw Stripe string rather than our internal
enum: this screen exists to show what Stripe thinks.

cancel_at.description:
Unix seconds. Set when a cancellation is scheduled, by whichever
mechanism (the flag, `cancel_at`, or the schedule).

resumable.description: The plan is set to end and Resume would keep it (never for a complimentary plan).

current_period_end.description:
Unix seconds. Read off the first subscription ITEM, not the
subscription: Stripe moved period boundaries onto items in the API
version this SDK pins, and `Subscription` no longer carries them.

oneOf.description: What Stripe charges: the subscription's default, else the customer's. Any type, not only cards.
A purchase waiting on its payment, if any.

money_outstanding.description:
Set while money is outstanding: only Pay now, Update card and Cancel
are offered, and this says why (SM7).

pagerduty_severity.description:
Severity of trigger events sent through this notification. Defaults
to `critical` when the caller omits it.

PagerDutySeverity.description:
`payload.severity` on trigger events. The user picks this per
notification; DOWN alerts default to `critical`.

PartnerBundle.description:
The named entitlement presets a partner may set on a client account.

Presets rather than free choice of packs: the partner pays a flat
wholesale rate per client, so what a client gets has to be one of the two
things that rate was priced against. A partner who needs something else
buys it retail on the client account or talks to us.

PartnerBundlePackSummary.description: One pack the client holds after the bundle was applied.

clients.description:
Live clients only, newest first. A soft-deleted client is absent, which
matches the `X-SQ-Account` switch refusing to open one.

PartnerClientMonitorTotals.description:
Monitor counts for one client, in the same state-aware sense
`GET /monitors/totals` uses: a paused monitor counts in `total` and
`paused` and in neither `online` nor `down`.

PartnerClientProductUsage.description:
One product's counters for one client.

Field-for-field the shape `/billing/usage` returns, on purpose: a partner
reading a client's usage here and that client reading their own usage in
the dashboard must not see two different numbers or two different units.

current_usage.description:
Usage in the product's CUSTOMER-FACING unit (see `unit`), not the raw
tracking unit: synthetic is metered in seconds and reported in minutes.

period.description: The period THIS product is metered in.

PartnerClientSummary.description: One managed client account, as the console lists it and as create answers.

account_id.description:
The client's account id. This is the value the partner sends as
`X-SQ-Account` to open the client in the ordinary dashboard.

contact_email.description:
Nullable because `accounts.primary_user_id` carries no foreign key; see
`DbPartnerChildAccount::contact_email`.

suspended.description:
Convenience mirror of `suspended_at.is_some()`, so a client list can
render the badge without parsing a timestamp.

PartnerClientUsageResponse.description:
Response for `GET /partner/accounts/{id}/usage`.

Deliberately carries NO top-level period. `/billing/usage` still has one
for backwards compatibility, and it is a lie whenever an account is
anchored on a different day per product: reporting one is what made the
2026-08-02 hard-stop incident invisible for a month. A new endpoint gets to
start correct.

products.description:
Every product, including the ones with no counter row yet, is NOT
guaranteed here: this lists the counter rows that exist, exactly as
`/billing/usage` does. A product a client has never used has no row.

label.description: Human label for the passkey (e.g., "iPhone 15 Pro").

public_key_credential_creation_options.description:
Opaque JSON string. The browser passes this straight to
`navigator.credentials.create()` after parsing.

PatchRumApplicationRequest.description: Body of `PATCH /rum/{app_id}`. Everything is optional; what is left out keeps its value.

domain.description: `null` clears the domain; leaving the field out keeps it.

settings.description:
Any subset of the settings: objects merge, others replace, `null` sets a nullable key.
Unknown keys are a 400; privacy, retention and body or header capture need an admin.

allowed_origins.description:
Origins allowed to send data (`https://app.example.com`, `https://*.example.com`,
`example.com`), at most 100. Empty allows all.

replay_monthly_target.description: Monthly replay target for Auto sampling; `null` clears it.

idempotency_key.description:
Client-generated, stable across retries of ONE pay attempt. Same
contract as the add-on endpoint: the same value twice is one charge.

payment_method_id.description: The saved card to charge. Omitted: Stripe charges the subscription default.

status.description:
`"paid"` when the charge went through, `"requires_action"` when the
customer's bank wants an authentication challenge finished in the
browser.

client_secret.description: Present only with `requires_action`. Feed it to the Payment Element.

customer_session_client_secret.description: With `requires_action`: lets the Payment Element offer the saved cards.

label.description: How to name it, for example "Visa ending 4242" or "Link (pat@example.com)".

brand.description: Card brand; empty for other types.

is_default.description: The method Stripe charges: the subscription's default, else the customer's.

is_expired.description:
True once the card's expiry month has passed. Surfaced so the list can
flag it before a renewal fails rather than after.

expires_soon.description:
True in the 30 days before the card expires, so it can be replaced
before a renewal fails.

PendingPurchase.description:
A purchase the customer started and has not paid for: "Complete payment"
or "Cancel purchase".

expires_at.description: Unix seconds after which Stripe drops it on its own.

PiiPattern.description: Patterns scrubbed from page text and free-text fields.

processors.description: Typed processor objects; unknown kinds and fields are rejected on save.

samples.description: At most 100 bounded records, with signal, id, timestamp_ns, body, fields, attributes, resource.

oneOf.description: When present, preview the last 100 matching stored logs or spans in this window.

retention_days.description:
Data-retention window this tier includes, in days. `null` for products
that have no retention dimension.

addon_key.description:
Add-on family, or `null` for a normal quota tier.

Clients MUST filter tier pickers to `addon_key == null`. Add-ons carry
the same `product` as the quota tiers they sit beside, so a picker that
filters on product alone offers them as if they were tiers, and
choosing one asks the server to replace the customer's paid pack.

purchasable.description: False for a pack off sale: holders keep and renew it, but no picker offers it.

slot.description:
`"tier"` (one per product, the plan picker), `"addon"` (`POST /billing/addons`) or
`"pack"` (bought by quantity beside the tier, such as status page extras).

entitlements.description: The entitlements matrix by scope; `packs` is keyed by pack id.

published_at.description: When it was last moved to `published`.

pack_id.description: A plan tier or an add-on pack.

quantity.description: Units of the pack, 1 to 100. Absent keeps what the account holds (1 for a new item).

effective_at.description: When the change takes effect. Absent for changes applied immediately.

amount_due_now_cents.description:
What Stripe charges today. For an upgrade this is the prorated
difference (Stripe's own preview of the immediate invoice); for a
downgrade it is always zero.

next_invoice_total_cents.description:
For an upgrade or a first purchase: the total of the invoice raised
today. For a downgrade: Stripe's total for the first invoice after
`effective_at` (zero when nothing more will be billed).

message.description: Why a `blocked` change cannot be made yet, or what `resume` does.

oneOf.description: For an upgrade: send this back on the confirm, so the charge is the one quoted.

quantity.description: The quantity this quote is for.

moves_to_interval.description: Set when the whole subscription moves to this interval (`month` or `year`).

PreviewWarning.description: Something the customer loses by making this change, or should know about it.

kind.description:
Stable machine key, so the client can style or order without parsing
the message.

PrivacyLevel.description:
A named privacy preset (design 7.1). `None` on [`RumPrivacySettings::level`] is the legacy
"Custom" level, where the individual masking flags apply.

current_usage.description:
Usage in the product's CUSTOMER-FACING unit (see `unit`), not the raw
tracking unit. Synthetic is metered in seconds for sub-minute accuracy
but reported in minutes so it matches the packs and the pricing page.

period.description:
The usage period THIS product is metered in. Products are anchored per
subscription, so an account can be metering RUM on its billing
anniversary while an unpurchased product runs on the calendar month;
the top-level `period` cannot describe that.

PublicDashboard.description: What `GET /public/dashboards/{token}` serves: no ids, authors or account details.

definition.description: Widgets not allowed on shares keep their place and title with an empty config.

timezone.description: The dashboard's zone; `null` follows the viewer's browser.

variables.description: Every dashboard variable, with how the viewer may use it.

PublicIncidentTemplate.description: What a service's incidents say on a status page (`services.public_incident_template`).

title.description: The public title; auto-published incidents never show the monitor's name.

message.description: The first public update when the incident is published.

logo_url.description: CDN URL, never an S3 key

logo_dark_url.description: The logo for the dark theme. Absent: the page shows `logo_url` in both.

title.description:
The title the page shows. Defaults to the current public title, then the service's
template; an auto-created incident never shows its monitor name.

message.description:
The first public update. Defaults to the service's template message when the incident
has no public update yet; otherwise nothing is posted.

notify_subscribers.description:
Email the page's subscribers that the incident opened (default true; never for a
resolved incident, and at most once per page).

PutSignupAttributionRequest.description:
Every field is optional and unknown fields are ignored. Text is trimmed, stripped of control
characters and cut to its cap; an empty value is absent.

oneOf.description: Write-once: fills only the columns that are still empty.
Replaces an earlier answer, including a skip.

skipped.description: Records a skip unless an answer exists. Not combinable with `self_reported`.

QuarantineReason.description: Why an address gets nothing. A complaint is never lifted automatically.

metric.description: Metrics source only: the metric name (or `$var`).

oneOf.description: Only `previous_period` is meaningful for a single value.

RangeSpec.description:
A window of T2 tokens (`now`, `now-2h`) or instants (ISO 8601, epoch milliseconds), resolved
when the query is compiled, so a stored view stays rolling.

ReachStatus.description: How well a page at one urgency reaches a target, best first.

oneOf.description: Set when the warning is about one urgency.

RecentChecksBatchRequest.description: Request body for the batched sparkline endpoint.

monitor_ids.description:
Monitor ids to fetch response-time samples for. Ids that are not HTTP
monitors, or that belong to another account, are simply absent from
the response.

status.description:
`"scheduled"`: the add-on stays until `effective_at`, the end of the
period already paid for, and is removed then with no credit or refund.

message.description: Text of the public "Reopened" update a published incident gets.

level_ids.description: Every level id of the policy exactly once, in the new order.

ReplayChunk.description: One downloadable piece of a page load.

start_ms.description: Unix ms of the first and last event.

snapshot.description: Starts with a full snapshot, so playback can start here.

ids.description: Chunk ids from the manifest (`b:`, `s:`) or stylesheet ids (`css:`), at most 20.

start_ms.description: Unix ms of the first and last recorded event (0 when nothing was recorded).

active_ms.description: Time with user input, over compacted blocks.

activity.description: `[start, end]` Unix ms ranges with user input, sorted and merged.

ReplayNoneReason.description: Why a session has no replay, as the SDK reported it.

ReplayPageLoad.description: One document in one tab, from navigation to unload.

url.description: The page URL when recording started, minimised (empty until known).

ReplayViewer.description: Who watched a session's replay, from the audit log.

views.description: Recorded views, at most one per viewer per 30 minutes.

viewers.description: Most recent first, over the audit log's 90-day read window.

index.description: 0 for the tab that recorded first.

post_public_update.description:
Post a public "Resolved" update even when the incident is not on a
status page. A published incident always gets one.

notify_subscribers.description: Email the status page subscribers (default true when published).

ResponseTimeDataPoint.description: One aggregate bucket on the dashboard response-time trends chart.

avg_ms.description: Average HTTP response time (ms) across all checks in the bucket.

p95_ms.description: 95th-percentile HTTP response time (ms) in the bucket.

ResponseTimeSeriesResponse.description:
Response for `GET /monitors/response-time-series`: the last 24h of
account-wide response-time aggregates in fixed-width buckets. Buckets
with no checks are absent rather than zero-filled.

interval_minutes.description: Width of each bucket in minutes.

RestartCharge.description: What the restarted plan charges today.

amount_due_cents.description: Charged today, net of any account credit, minor units.

renews_at.description: Unix seconds: when the restarted plan first renews.

stripe_subscription_id.description: The plan being restarted; send it back on the confirm.

voided.description: Voided first, oldest first: nothing more is owed on them.

idempotency_key.description: Client-generated, stable across retries of one restart.

customer_session_client_secret.description: Lets the payment sheet offer the saved cards.

version.description: The dashboard's current version, for optimistic concurrency.

interval_seconds.description: Absent for widgets that are not bucketed.

RotationAnchorResponse.description: The local date of one handoff and the participant (0-based index) who starts there.

RuleCapture.description: What a matching session records. Replay implies Analyze.

oneOf.description:
The page URL, checked on each view. `regex` values use the common subset of the
Rust and JavaScript syntaxes, at most 256 characters, with no nested quantifiers.
A custom event (`addAction`) with this name.
A non-ignored error, optionally narrowed by type, message fragment or handling.
A failed request of this class, optionally to a URL containing `url_contains`.
A frustration signal.
A final vital above `gt` (milliseconds for LCP and INP, unitless for CLS).
`setUser` was called with an id. A struct variant so unknown fields are refused.
A global attribute or user trait equals `value`.
The device class at init.
The release passed at init.
The environment passed at init.

RuleCondition.description: One condition of a rule (design 6.2). A rule matches when all of its conditions hold.

RumAccountSettings.description:
Account-wide RUM access (`GET`, `PUT /rum/settings`). Viewers and auditors never see replay
content or network bodies, whatever this says.

body_access.description: Who may read network bodies, headers and console arguments.

RumAccountSettingsUpdate.description: `PUT /rum/settings`: fields left out keep their value.

RumAlertQuery.description:
A RUM alert rule (Wave 2 design 5.13, 6.10). Issue triggers fire per issue event; threshold
and metric triggers are windowed like log and metric rules.

filters.description: Filters in the RUM grammar (`common::rum::filter`): issue fields for issue triggers.

oneOf.description: What threshold and metric triggers measure.

action_interval_seconds.description: Minimum seconds between notifications per issue for issue triggers. Default 3600.

allowed_origins.description: Origins allowed to send data; empty allows all.

replay_monthly_target.description: Monthly replay target that Auto sampling aims for, when set.

config_revision.description: Revision of the published SDK config; increases on every settings or rule change.

data_region.description: Where the application's data is stored (`us`).

retention.description:
The customer's own maximum retention for this application's data, in
days. Absent, and by default, means no limit beyond the account's
entitlement. See `common::retention::ceiling`: the entitlement is a MAX
over the account's packs, which makes every window a floor, and this is
the only thing that lets a customer go below it.

capture.description:
Network, console, error and canvas capture (Wave 2). Omitted while default, like every
Wave 2 key: see `rum_settings`.

routes.description: Route rules applied at ingest before automatic id collapse.

observe_sample_rate.description: Share of sessions that send Observe data, 0 to 1. Default 1.

allow_requests_without_origin.description: Accept ingest requests without an `Origin` header (server-side senders).

resource_exclusions.description:
Resource URLs not recorded as resource events: a path on the page's origin
("/api/heartbeat") or an absolute http(s) URL ("https://analytics.example.com"). At most 50.

frustration_ignore_selectors.description:
CSS selectors whose clicks never count as rage or dead clicks, delivered to the SDK.
Whitespace around each is trimmed and empty or repeated entries are dropped; then at most
50 remain, each up to 256 characters with no control characters, else the save is a 400.

RumCaptureSettings.description: What the SDK captures beyond views and errors.

console.description: Console levels recorded. Default: error and warn.

oneOf.description: Present on writes. Queue acceptance is not delivery confirmation.

body.description: Plain text, 1 to 10000 characters. Not HTML.

at_ms.description: Absolute UTC epoch milliseconds, only for session comments.

mentions.description: Account user IDs, at most 20 distinct recipients.

RumContentAccess.description: Who may watch replays in an account (design 7.3, J6). Viewers and auditors never can.

timestamp.description: The session's first occurrence in the range.

has_replay.description: Whether the session has a recorded replay.

error_ts_ms.description: `timestamp` in Unix milliseconds, to seek the replay to.

event_id.description: Event id of that first occurrence.

user_count.description: Distinct identified users in the range.

affected_sessions.description: The 50 sessions that hit the error most recently.

interval.description: Timeline bucket width: `5m`, `1h`, `6h` or `1d`. Derived from the range when absent.

tz.description:
IANA time zone timeline buckets align to. Default `UTC`; a name the server does not know
also means UTC, while a malformed one is a 400.

timestamp.description: Bucket start; buckets without errors carry a count of 0.

to.description: ISO 8601 end of the range. Default: now.

resolved.description: Accepted and ignored: error groups have no resolved state.

search.description: Case-insensitive substring of any error message in the group.

RumEventGroup.description: What a collapsed row stands for.

rows.description: Stored rows folded into this one.

count.description: Occurrences: request counts for aggregated requests, repeats for console lines.

last_offset_ms.description: Offset of the last folded row.

RumFacets.description: Up to 50 non-empty values per dimension, by listed sessions active in the range.

from.description: ISO 8601. Sessions active in `[from, to]` are counted. Default: 30 days before `to`.

field.description:
Comma-separated lists to fill: `browser`, `os`, `country`, `device_type`, `region`,
`release`, `env`, `route`, `channel`, `referrer_host`, `sdk_version`. Default: the first
four; lists not asked for are empty (the first four) or absent.

q.description: Case-insensitive substring the values must contain, for autocomplete.

f.description:
Session filters in the RUM filter grammar, repeatable. A list ignores the filters on its
own field, so every value stays pickable.

config_last_accepted_ms.description: Config GETs are served by the CDN and are not in ingest statistics.

limitations.description: Invalid credentials cannot safely be attributed to an application.

last_seen_at.description: Newest measure in the last 24 hours; null when there is none.

auto_resolve_days.description: Open issues with no events for this many days are resolved. `null` turns it off.

session_count.description:
Sessions with a page view in the range; approximate (within about 1%) above a few
thousand.

avg_lcp_ms.description: Deprecated: mean of one value per page view. Use `p75_lcp_ms`.

avg_fcp_ms.description: Deprecated: mean of one value per page view. Use `p75_fcp_ms`.

avg_cls.description: Deprecated: mean of one value per page view. Use `p75_cls`.

avg_inp_ms.description: Deprecated: mean of one value per page view. Use `p75_inp_ms`.

avg_ttfb_ms.description: Deprecated: mean of one value per page view. Use `p75_ttfb_ms`.

error_session_count.description: Sessions counted in `session_count` with at least one error event in the range.

p75_lcp_ms.description: 75th percentile over one value per page view; null without samples.

vitals_sample_rate.description:
Share of page views the vitals, distribution and top page vitals were computed from:
1 below 400,000 views in the range, else a uniform sample with counts scaled back.

session_query.description: Pass verbatim to the Sessions list to preserve view-cohort membership.

bounce_rate.description: Fraction from 0 to 1. One-view sessions with under 10 seconds active time.

approximate.description:
True when these numbers come from the daily rollup (large applications, windows of at
least 3 days, filters on device class, device, browser, OS or country only). The window
then starts at the UTC midnight nearest `from` (`session_query` and `previous` follow
it), a window ending within 20 minutes of now counts today up to the last 15-minute
refresh, sessions and visitors are estimates (about 1%), page and session metrics use
each view's latest sample within its UTC day, and `top_pages[].url` holds routes.

previous.description:
The same fields for the preceding window, without its own `previous`.
Typed as an object so the spec has no self-reference for docs renderers.

filters.description: Filters to apply to the Sessions list.

mask_inputs.description:
Mask the value of every form input before it leaves the browser.
Defaults to ON.

mask_text.description:
Mask all user-visible page text. Defaults to OFF: a replay with every
text node masked is unreadable, so this is opt-in. Anything the page
renders is therefore recorded verbatim unless the customer turns this
on, and every document that describes replay has to say so.

hide_action_text.description:
Name clicks by tag and class only, never by element text. Defaults to
OFF. When on, the ingestor also drops click names an SDK sends anyway.

oneOf.description: Wave 2 privacy preset; `None` is the legacy "Custom" level where the flags above apply.

pii_patterns.description: Patterns scrubbed from page text and free text. None for legacy applications.

never_record_urls.description: URL patterns where replay pauses and Analyze events drop.

honor_gpc.description: Treat Global Privacy Control as an opt-out. Off for legacy applications.

capture_user_email.description: Keep the email passed to `setUser`. On by default.

account_usage.description: The account's canonical billing counter, shared by its applications.

applications.description: Up to 100 current applications in the caller's account, ordered by claim count.

sample_rate.description: The configured rate, 0.00001 to 1. For an Auto rule, the most Auto may set.

auto_sample.description: Auto: the rate follows the replay quota, recomputed hourly (Replay rules only).

effective_sample_rate.description:
The rate the SDK uses when the sampling tick has set one: the Auto rate, or a lowered
rate for an error rule when errored sessions alone would exhaust the replay quota.

conditions.description: All must hold. Empty means every session.

min_duration_ms.description: Sampled recordings upload only once the session is this old. Error conditions bypass it.

require_interaction.description: Sampled recordings upload only after a user interaction. Error conditions bypass it.

RumRetentionCeiling.description:
A customer's requested maximum retention, in days, for one RUM application.

`None` on a field means "no ceiling for this product": the account's
entitlement stands.

session_replay_days.description: Replay retention ceiling, 7, 14 or 30 days, capped by the account entitlement.

RumRouteRule.description:
A customer route rule: URLs matching `pattern` (`/profiles/:id`) get its route, named
`name` when given.

RumRuleAttributionCoverage.description: Retained session activity, not a completeness guarantee or a billing counter.

session_retention_days.description:
Current lower bound for replay summary retention: max(Observe, Replay).
Older rows can have different retention, and deleted data cannot be recovered.

retention_limited.description:
True when current retention shortens the requested billing-period window.
False does not guarantee historical completeness.

RumRulePreview.description: What a rule would record, from the last 7 days of sessions (`POST .../rules/preview`).

sessions_in_window.description: Sessions the application had in the window.

matching_sessions_in_window.description: Of those, sessions the conditions and gates would match, before sampling.

sample_rate.description: The sample rate applied: the configured rate, or the current Auto rate.

estimated_sessions_per_month.description: Matching sessions scaled to a 30-day month, after sampling.

quota_product.description: `session_replay` for Replay rules, `rum_analyze` for Analyze rules.

monthly_quota.description: The account's monthly quota for that product.

quota_share.description: `estimated_sessions_per_month / monthly_quota`; null when there is no quota.

approximate.description:
True when part of the rule could not be evaluated exactly from stored sessions; the
estimate is then an upper bound.

not_evaluated.description: Condition kinds and gates counted as always true.

query.description: URL query string only, at most 4096 characters. No absolute URLs.

outdated.description: Unknown or unparseable SDK versions have no age assessment.

events.description:
Detail events and page views (`type: "view"`), oldest first, at most 2,000 rows and
2.5 MB of JSON; page through `/sessions/{session_id}/events` for the rest.

views.description: Page views, oldest first, at most 1,000 (`views_truncated`).

counts.description: Stored rows per kind over the whole session, as `/events` returns them uncollapsed.

utm.description: `source`, `medium`, `campaign`, `content` and `term`, when the first page view had them.

attributes.description: The session's latest global attributes, without the reserved `sq.` keys.

user_name.description: The name passed to `setUser`, within the 30-day identity window.

traits.description: The traits passed to `setUser`, within the 30-day identity window.

other_session_count.description:
Other sessions of the same user (or anonymous visitor, without a user) that started up
to 30 days before or after this one.

id.description: The event id, or a stable id derived from the row for kinds stored without one.

window_id.description: Null when the SDK sent no window.

page_url.description: The page the event happened on; empty when unknown.

oneOf.description: Present on a collapsed row that stands for more than one stored row.

RumSessionEvent.description: One event of the session, in the shape of the ingest kinds (design 6.3).

RumSessionEventCounts.description: Stored events per kind, once per event; `custom` counts custom events.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; absent on the last page.

counts.description:
Rows per kind over the whole session for this `q` and `collapse`, whatever `kinds`,
`from_ms`, `to_ms` and `cursor` say. Kinds without rows are absent.

bodies_withheld.description:
True when the caller lacks body access: request and response bodies and headers and
console messages are left out.

kinds.description:
Comma-separated kinds to return: `view`, `view_end`, `custom`, `action`, `error`,
`network`, `resource`, `console`, `long_frame`, `status`. Default: all.

from_ms.description: Lower bound, inclusive, in milliseconds from the session's start.

to_ms.description: Upper bound, inclusive, in milliseconds from the session's start.

q.description:
Case-insensitive substring of a URL, route, request URL, error type or message, action
name or selector, custom event name or console message (console messages need body
access).

collapse.description:
`true` folds repeated successful requests, resources and identical console lines of one
page view into their first row, with `group` saying how many it stands for.

cursor.description: `next_cursor` of the previous page; the other parameters must be the same.

limit.description: Page size, default 500, at most 1,000. A page also stops at about 2.5 MB of JSON.

total.description: Every session matching the query, exact.

total_with_replay.description: Sessions in `total` with a replay that can still be played.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; absent on the last page.

from.description: ISO 8601. Sessions active in `[from, to]` are listed. Default: 30 days before `to`.

search.description:
Case-insensitive match on any user id or email the session carried, a session id prefix,
any visited URL or any error message in the session.

url.description: Case-insensitive substring of any URL the session visited. Same as `f=url:contains:<value>`.

error_fingerprint.description: Only sessions with an error event in this group. Same as `f=error_issue:eq:<value>`.

has_error.description: `true` keeps sessions with at least one error event.

has_replay.description: `true` keeps sessions with a replay that can still be played.

has_frustration.description:
`true` keeps sessions carrying at least one frustration signal (rage, dead or error
click). `false` and absent mean no filter.

sort.description:
`started` (default), `duration`, `active_time`, `errors`, `frustration` (the score),
`friction` (rage, dead and error clicks) or `pages`.

offset.description: Rows to skip, at most 10,000. Prefer `cursor`; the two cannot be combined.

f.description:
Filters in the RUM filter grammar, `<field>:<op>[:<value>]`, repeatable, at most 20. All
must hold. See the RUM reference for the fields and operators.

cursor.description:
`next_cursor` of the previous page. The query must otherwise be the same; `from` and `to`
may be left out, and then come from the cursor.

cohort.description: Opaque analytics cohort from a returned `session_query`. Keeps exact view membership.

first_seen.description: Earliest measure, event or replay segment of the session.

last_seen.description: Latest measure, event or replay segment of the session.

rage_click_count.description:
Frustration signals the SDK detects on click actions and stores in
`rum_events.frustration`. Always present, never null: a session with
none reports 0.

`serde(default)` is deserialization-side robustness only. The
serializer always emits these, so `schema(required = true)` keeps the
generated OpenAPI honest: without it utoipa infers optional from the
serde default and the published contract disagrees with the real one.

action_count.description:
Total user actions in the session, summed from `rum_measures`.

Reads 0 for sessions recorded by SDKs that hardcode `action_count: 0` on
their measures. Not rendered in the dashboard for that reason.

duration_ms.description: `last_seen` minus `first_seen`, over the session's whole lifetime.

entry_url.description: URL of the session's first page view.

active_ms.description: Time the user was active (input, visible tab); 0 when the SDK reported none.

failed_request_count.description: Requests with status 0 or 400 and above.

frustration_score.description:
0 to 100: `round(100 * (1 - exp(-(3 * rage + 2 * error clicks + dead + 2 * errors +
failed requests) / 10)))`. The inputs are the counts on this row.

entry_route.description: Route of the first page view; empty when unknown.

exit_url.description: URL of the last page view.

replay_reason.description:
Why there is no replay: `expired` (past the replay retention), or the SDK's reason:
`not_sampled`, `consent`, `gpc`, `opted_out`, `privacy_url`, `too_large`,
`request_budget`. Absent when there is a replay or no reason is known.

window_count.description: Browser tabs the session used; 0 when the SDK sent no window.

viewed_by_me.description: The caller watched this session's replay in the last 90 days.

RumSessionView.description: One page view, with its latest valid vitals.

error_count.description: Error events on this page view, repeats included.

RumSessionWindow.description: One browser tab of the session.

RumSourceMap.description: One source map recorded against a release.

original_file.description:
The name the map was uploaded under, which symbolication matches
against the file name in each stack frame.

source_map_count.description:
Source maps recorded against this release. A release that was just
created has none.

from.description: ISO 8601 lower bound, inclusive. Every RUM range is at most 90 days and not reversed.

url.description: Case-insensitive substring of the page URL.

samples.description: Page views with a valid value.

RumVitalsDistribution.description: Page views per Web Vital, split by Google's good / needs improvement / poor thresholds.

interval.description: Bucket width: `5m`, `1h`, `6h` or `1d`. Derived from the range when absent.

tz.description:
IANA time zone buckets align to, for example `America/Denver`. Default `UTC`; a name the
server does not know also means UTC, while a malformed one is a 400.

url.description: Case-insensitive substring of the page URL.

SamlConnectionResponse.description:
SAML connection as returned to the dashboard. Combines our row (account
linkage, claimed domain) with the live Stytch object (SP-side values the
customer pastes into the IdP, plus the configured IdP values).

status.description: `pending` until the IdP side is configured, then `active`.

acs_url.description: Service-provider values for the IdP side of the setup.

idp_entity_id.description: Configured IdP values (echoed back so the UI can show current state).

has_certificate.description: Whether at least one verification certificate is on file.

email_domain_verified.description:
Whether the account has a current DNS verification for `email_domain`.
The sign-in screen routes only a verified domain.

late_data_seconds.description: Recompute this bounded recent interval; older late data never reissues a notification.

query.description: Serialized explorer state. Relative times stay relative when the view is opened.

ScheduledChangeResponse.description: What this plan changes to at the end of the billing period.

pack_id.description:
The pack it changes to, or `null` when the product returns to its
free tier.

ScimConnectionResponse.description:
SCIM connection as returned to the dashboard. Never carries the bearer
token; only the last four characters.

base_url.description: SCIM base URL the customer pastes into their IdP.

ScimConnectionWithTokenResponse.description: Create / rotate response: carries the bearer token exactly once.

bearer_token.description: Full bearer token. Shown once, never stored, never retrievable again.

console.description: Console levels recorded, after the privacy level's limit.

SdkConfigPaused.description: What a deleted application publishes, so SDKs still running stop sending (5.8).

SdkConfigV2.description: Config v2 for an active application (6.2).

revision.description: Increases on every publish. Also sent as the object's `x-amz-meta-revision`.

rules.description: Enabled rules, in position order. Rules combine with ANY.

suppressed_keys.description: `error_key` values (6.3) of suppressed issues; the SDK drops matching errors.

dnr.description: The application has a do-not-record list; the SDK checks identities (6.3).

sample_rate.description: Share of sessions that send Observe data.

SdkPrivacyConfig.description: Effective privacy (7.1): the level's rules applied to the stored flags.

level.description: `strict`, `balanced`, `relaxed`, or `custom` for applications that predate levels.

block_media.description: Strict blocks images, video and SVG behind sized placeholders.

SdkRule.description: One rule as the SDK evaluates it (5.4).

id.description: The rule id; the SDK samples with `fnv1a32(session_id + ":" + id)`.

sample_rate.description:
The rate in force: the Auto rate for Auto rules, the throttled rate for an error rule the
sampling tick has slowed, otherwise the configured rate.

children.description: Members while collapsed (Grafana row model); empty when expanded.

channel.description:
One of `search`, `ai_assistant`, `community`, `social`, `referral`, `content`,
`review_site`, `github_mcp`, `other`. A skip goes through `skipped`.

in_maintenance.description: A maintenance window naming this service is running now. It holds paging, never the status.

failing_monitor_count.description: Linked monitors failing now; paused ones are left out.

last_incident_at.description: When the newest incident on the service opened.

on_call_now.description: The service's on-call schedule, else every user and schedule on the policy's first level.

ServiceHealthStatus.description: The worst of incident and monitor state. Maintenance never changes it.

total_incidents.description: Incidents opened in the window, merged ones left out.

status.description: The monitor's own status label, such as `success`, `failed`, `bad` or `expired`.

healthy.description: Whether the monitor counts as healthy for auto-resolve.

details.description:
Stored details with a webhook URL cut to its host; a Slack token reads
back as `has_token: true`.

ServiceOnCall.description: One person on call for a service right now.

schedule_id.description: The schedule that puts them on call; absent for a user named on the policy directly.

until.description: When the schedule hands off; absent for a direct user or past 90 days.

ServicePage.description: One page of services: `data` stays the bare array.

total.description: Services matching the filters, across every page.

next_cursor.description: Pass back as `cursor` for the next page; `null` on the last.

incident_merge_window_minutes.description: Deprecated and unused: every failure joins the service's open auto incident.

reopen_window_minutes.description: A failure this many minutes after a resolved auto incident's last alert reopens it; 0 never does.

auto_resolve.description: Whether an auto-created incident resolves itself once every monitor recovers.

oneOf.description: Prefills Publish and words auto-published incidents.

owner_team.description: The team that owns the service; filter the list with `team`.

tags.description: Free-form labels; filter the list with `tag`.

on_call_schedule_id.description: Who is on call for this service; without it, the escalation policy's first level.

oneOf.description: The roll-up of incidents, monitors, maintenance and on call. On the list and get routes.

percentage.description: Share of the window with no open incident on the service; null for an empty window.

incident_seconds.description: Seconds with at least one open incident.

measured_seconds.description: Seconds measured: the window after the service was created, up to now.

redirect_path.description: Sanitized at start; absent on the doors that never take one.

SessionResponse.description: A session from a login, plus where the frontend should land.

packs.description: The packs the bundle grants, with the catalog ids they resolved to.

granted.description:
How many partner-sourced entitlement rows this call created. Zero when
the client was already on the bundle, which is what makes the endpoint
safe to call repeatedly.

cancelled.description:
How many partner-sourced entitlement rows this call cancelled, i.e.
what the previous bundle had that this one does not. Rows sourced from
Stripe or from a staff grant are never counted here because they are
never touched.

status.description: What the public page shows for this component, whatever its monitor says.

note.description: Shown next to the status on the public page. Up to 500 characters, one line.

expires_at.description: When the override lapses on its own. Must be in the future. Leave out to keep it until cleared.

allowed_times.description: Presets a viewer may pick, from `15m 1h 4h 1d 2d 7d 30d 90d`.

ShareVariable.description:
How a public viewer may use one variable. A variable the share does not list is locked to
the dashboard default.

allowed.description:
The values a viewer may pick; `null` allows every value (and All when the variable
includes it).

Signal.description: A telemetry signal, as the authorizer scopes and meters it.

SignupAttributionStatus.description: What the dashboard needs to decide whether to send a first touch or show the question.

eligible.description: The caller is the account owner and the account is at most 14 days old.

has_first_touch.description: A first touch is already stored, so the client need not send one.

answered.description: An answer is stored. A skip counts as one.

SilentMonitor.description: An active monitor whose outage would reach no one.

SilentMonitors.description: The account's silent monitors (first 100 by name) and the one-time banner state.

total.description: Every silent active monitor, not just the ones listed.

has_default_group.description: Whether new monitors get a default group when created without group ids.

SingleLocationReason.description: Why a new HTTP monitor starts on one location rather than the default pair.

SlaMonth.description: Attainment of one calendar month against the monitor's target.

month.description: "YYYY-MM" (UTC calendar month; the newest month is partial).

uptime_percentage.description:
Average of daily uptime percentages, 3 decimals. `null` when the
month has no check data.

attained.description: `uptime >= target`; `null` when there is no data to judge.

authorize_url.description: Open this in the browser. It carries a signed, single-use `state`.

idempotency_key.description:
Client-generated, stable across retries of ONE confirm attempt. Same
contract as `POST /billing/addons`: the same value twice is one charge.

client_secret.description:
Hand this to Stripe's Payment Element to collect and confirm the card.
Credits land when the invoice-paid webhook arrives.

customer_session_client_secret.description: Lets the Payment Element offer the saved cards, so a top-up does not ask for the card again.

intervals.description: Bucket sizes in seconds the source can serve, ascending.

SsoAuthenticateRequest.description: Body for `POST /login/sso`, which completes the SSO redirect.

token.description:
The `token` query param Stytch appends to the login redirect URL when
`stytch_token_type=sso`.

SsoStartResponse.description:
Response for `POST /auth/sso/start`.

Enumeration-safe by construction: the shape is identical whether or not
the domain has SSO, and the status code is always 200. `redirect_url` is
`null` when there is no startable connection, which covers "no such
account", "account without SSO", and "SSO configured but not yet active"
with one indistinguishable answer.

redirect_url.description: Stytch SSO start URL to redirect the browser to, or `null`.

StackFrame.description: One stack frame, innermost first. Stored as JSON on error rows and returned by the API.

function.description: The engine's function name as printed (`Object.onSave`, `mount/<`, `async loadPage`).

file.description: Script URL or source path, or an engine marker such as `<anonymous>` or `[native code]`.

in_app.description: Whether the frame is the customer's own code (see [`is_in_app_location`]).

invoices.description: Voided by the start over, oldest first: nothing more is owed on them.

amount_cents.description: What is left to pay on them together, minor units.

currency.description: ISO 4217, uppercase; `null` when nothing is outstanding.

idempotency_key.description: Client-generated, stable across retries of one start over.

invoices_left.description: Still open after a failed void; voided by the nightly tick.

counters.description: Drop counters since the previous status.

StatusOverride.description:
A status the owner forced on a component. The public page shows it, and the note, instead
of what the monitor says.

expires_at.description: When it lapses on its own, or null to keep it until cleared.

page_url.description:
Where the public page lives: the custom domain once it is active,
otherwise the page's address on statuspage.siteqwality.com.

logo_url.description: CDN URLs of the assets above, for previews.

friendly_name.description: The name the page shows. Up to 256 characters.

cname_target.description:
The intermediate CNAME the customer must point their domain at,
e.g. "<status_page_id>.custom.siteqwality.com"

acm_validation.description: ACM DNS validation records, needed while status = "pending_validation"

oneOf.description: The last check of a live domain; absent until the first one, a few minutes after it goes live.
Absent for our own hostnames, which always mail from the default sender.

billing_interval.description: `"month"` or `"year"`; must match the rest of the subscription.

idempotency_key.description: Client-generated, stable across retries of one confirm attempt.

quantity.description: Units to hold, 0 to 100. Zero removes the extra at the end of the period.

oneOf.description: From the quote. Required when the quantity goes up on a live plan.

groups.description: In the order the page shows them.

whole_page.description: Covers the whole page; `affected_http_job_ids` is then empty.

StatusPageSubscriber.description: Someone who asked for email about a status page.

state.description:
`confirmed` receives notices. `pending` has not clicked the link yet. `queued` was
imported and waits for its confirmation email. `expired` never clicked, and the link
lapsed. `quarantined` bounced or complained and gets nothing.

subscribed_at.description: When the address was first submitted.

component_ids.description: Components (monitor ids) whose notices it gets. Empty means every component.

kinds.description: Kinds of update it gets. Empty means both.

oneOf.description: How the address was added. Absent on subscribers from before it was recorded.

consent_version.description: The version of the confirm page wording it agreed to, set when it confirms.

StepUpAction.description: A sensitive action that may need a fresh email step-up.

queued.description: Imported addresses waiting for their confirmation email.

quarantined.description: Bounced or complained. They get no mail and hold no place.

SubscriberPage.description:
One page of subscribers. `data` stays the bare array like every other list;
the rest rides beside it.

total.description: Subscribers matching the filters, not the length of `data`.

counts.description: The whole list by state, whatever the filters.

capacity.description: The most subscribers a page can hold (confirmed, pending and queued together).

SubscriberState.description:
Where a subscription stands. `Expired` is a sign-up whose link lapsed unconfirmed; a daily job purges it.
`Queued` waits for its confirmation email. `Quarantined` bounced or complained and gets nothing.

complimentary.description:
True when this plan is covered by the account's complimentary grant:
Stripe bills it at $0, so the UI shows the list price struck through.

oneOf.description:
A downgrade (or removal) Stripe will apply at the end of the current
billing period, or `null` when nothing is scheduled.

billed_cents.description:
What Stripe bills for a legacy plan row (its legacy price on one row, 0 on the rows it
includes). `null` for other rows, which bill their pack's price.

Symbolication.description:
How a frame was symbolicated through a source map (5.7, step 3). `None` on a frame means
symbolication was not attempted.

columns.description: Empty means one number column per visible query and formula.

user_id.description: The user paged: the target user, or whoever is on call now for a schedule.

name.description: The user's name (or email), or the schedule's name.

on_call_name.description: For a schedule, the on-call user's name (or email).

problem.description: Why nobody can be paged at all: `user_removed`, `schedule_removed` or `nobody_on_call`.

incident_id.description: Acknowledgement and resolution use the existing /incident/{id} actions.

renotify_seconds.description: Zero disables reminders. Timers use evaluated input time, never retries.

until.description: Required only for mute, at most 30 days from now. RFC 3339 UTC.

oneOf.description: Observed monitor health seconds, excluding maintenance and unobserved minutes.

has_data.description: Whether the account already has data for the template's main source.

requires.description: Every source the template reads, main source first.

port.description: Port the TLS check connects to.

cipher_suite.description:
`None` means our rustls probe could not complete, i.e. the endpoint
offers only ciphers modern clients have dropped. The check itself runs
on native-tls and still succeeds.

error.description:
One of the RFC 6749 error codes: `invalid_request`, `invalid_client`,
`invalid_scope`, `unsupported_grant_type`, `temporarily_unavailable`.

error_description.description:
Human-readable detail. Never distinguishes "unknown client" from
"wrong secret": both are `invalid_client` with the same description.

access_token.description: The bearer token to send as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

expires_in.description: Lifetime in seconds, passed through from the issuer.

scope.description: Space-delimited granted scopes. Absent when the token carries none.

url.description:
The page URL; the route (such as `/products/:id`) when the Overview is
`approximate`.

avg_lcp_ms.description: Deprecated: mean of one value per page view. Use `p75_lcp_ms`.

avg_load_time_ms.description: Deprecated: mean of one value per initial page load. Use `p75_load_time_ms`.

p75_load_time_ms.description: Initial page loads only; route changes carry no load time.

vitals_samples.description: Page views with at least one of LCP, INP or CLS.

sort_by.description: A query or formula id; defaults to the first visible one.

totp_code.description: 6-digit code from the user's authenticator app.

TotpDisableRequest.description: `DELETE /account/security/totp`: a current code, or a `disable_totp` step-up grant.

qr_code_url.description: `otpauth://` URL, rendered as a QR code on the client.

recovery_codes.description: One-time recovery codes. Shown once; never recoverable.

UnifiedMonitor.description:
One row of the unified monitor list.

Fields are emitted as explicit `null` rather than omitted when they do not
apply to the row's type. The dashboard reads several of them positionally
(an absent `method` and a null `method` are not the same thing to it), and
bulk edit spreads the whole row back into an update request, so a missing
key is a silently blanked setting rather than a cosmetic difference.

friendly_name.description:
Display name. Browser checks store this as `name`; it is projected here
so one column renderer serves all three types.

paused_reason.description: Why a paused monitor is paused: `user` or `dormancy` (older rows may say `billing`).

oneOf.description:
Set on an ACTIVE monitor that is not being checked: `quota` while the
account's quota for its product is used up. Show this instead of `current_status`.

uptime_24h.description:
Uptime percentage over the last 24h. HTTP monitors only, and null when
the monitor has no checks in the window.

group_notifications.description: Notification groups, resolved in one batched query for the whole page.

notifies_no_one.description:
True when an outage would reach no one: no attached notification group has a
channel, and no linked service opens incidents automatically with someone to page.

timeout_ms.description:
Milliseconds. Browser checks store seconds; the value is converted so
the Timeout column reads true for them instead of blanking.

method.description:
Explicitly null for heartbeats and browser checks. The dashboard's
legacy "no method means heartbeat" heuristic still exists as a
fallback, so this must be present and null rather than omitted.

has_auth.description:
True when a basic-auth password or bearer token is stored for this
monitor. The credentials themselves are write-only and are deliberately
absent from this struct, so there is nothing here for a read-only
viewer, a scoped API key, an M2M client or a read-only impersonation
session to read back. See `crate::model::api::secrets`.

Bulk edit spreads a row back into an update request, and the update
statement writes `COALESCE($n, auth_password)`, so an absent key leaves
the stored credential alone. That is why these two can be dropped from
the shape outright rather than emitted as null.

custom_http_headers.description:
Names and allowlisted metadata values; other values become `secrets::REDACTED`.
Sending the placeholder back on an update keeps the stored value.

UpdateActionItemRequest.description: PATCH semantics: an absent field is left unchanged; `null` clears a nullable one.

due_date.description: Changing the date or the owner re-arms the one overdue reminder.

service_id.description: `null` unlinks the service; leaving the field out keeps it.

confirmation_threshold.description:
Consecutive failed runs (by the location quorum) before the check is
DOWN, 1 to 10. Omitted or `null` means 1.

rerun_on_failure.description:
Rerun a failed run once from the same location before it counts. The
rerun uses synthetic minutes. Omitted or `null` means off.

service_id.description: The service this monitor belongs to; `null` detaches it and omission keeps it.

UpdateDashboardRequest.description: A whole-document save. `version` is the version the edit started from.

locked.description: Only the creator and admins may change it; absent keeps it.

UpdateDnsJobRequest.description:
Body of `PUT /dns/job/{dns_job_id}`.

`manual_expiry_date` is REQUIRED, and `null` is how it is cleared. It is
deliberately not `#[serde(default)]`: with exactly one field, an omitted key
would silently clear the customer's date, and `{}` deserializing into
"delete what I typed" is not a request anybody meant to make. An empty body
is a 422 from the shared `Json` extractor instead.

manual_expiry_date.description:
RFC 3339. Must be in the future and inside
[`MAX_MANUAL_EXPIRY_YEARS`] years. Send `null` to clear it.

`required` is asserted explicitly because utoipa reads an `Option<T>` as
an optional key while serde, with no `#[serde(default)]`, demands it. The
published spec has to say what the endpoint actually does.

service_id.description: The service this monitor belongs to; `null` detaches it and omission keeps it.

oneOf.description: Leaving `escalate_to_policy` clears `escalate_to_policy_id`.

escalate_to_policy_id.description: Allowed only when the policy ends up with `on_exhausted: escalate_to_policy`.

oneOf.description: Preferred HTTP version for the check client.

confirmation_threshold.description:
Number of consecutive failed checks (1-10) required before the monitor
is considered down and notifications are sent.

tls_port.description:
Port the TLS check connects to, 1 to 65535. Omitted keeps the stored
port (443 for a new TLS check). Needs `monitor_tls`.

recovery_period_runs.description: Healthy runs in a row (1-10) before a recovery is notified.

flap_hold.description: Deprecated: sets `flap_hold_override` when that is absent.

flap_hold_override.description: Absent leaves it unchanged; `null` follows the account's notification setting.

service_id.description: The service this monitor belongs to; `null` detaches it and omission keeps it.

oneOf.description: Null or absent derives it from the incident's severity.

UpdateIncidentRequest.description: PATCH semantics: an absent field is left unchanged.

oneOf.description:
Deprecated: post an update, or call resolve or reopen. `resolved`
resolves (with a public update); other values set the public status.

resolved_at.description: Deprecated and ignored: resolving stamps the time.

public_title.description: The title status pages show; `null` clears it so they show `title`.

service_id.description: Move the incident to this service; `null` detaches it.

UpdateKind.description: The kinds of update a subscriber can choose between.

UpdateManualComponent.description: Fields left out keep their values.

UpdateNotificationGroupRequest.description: PATCH-style: a field left out keeps its stored value, and `null` or 0 clears it.

is_default.description: `true` makes this the account's default group; `false` on the default leaves the account without one.

UpdatePostmortemRequest.description: PATCH semantics: an absent field is left unchanged.

oneOf.description: `published` needs a resolved incident.

owner_user_id.description: A member of the account; `null` clears it.

domain.description: `null` clears the domain; leaving the field out keeps it.

oneOf.description: Keys given replace the stored values (nested objects merge); keys left out keep theirs.

UpdateRumRecordingRuleRequest.description:
Body of `PUT /rum/{app_id}/rules/{rule_id}`. Every field is optional: one left out keeps
its stored value, and the result is validated as a whole.

conditions.description: Replaces the whole list when given.

UpdateSamlConnectionRequest.description:
Body for `PUT /account/sso/saml/connection`. Every field is optional;
only supplied fields are forwarded to Stytch.

Two ways to configure the IdP side: paste a `metadata_url` (Stytch fetches
entity id, SSO URL, and certificate) or fill the three fields by hand.

clear_email_domain.description: Set true to release the claimed domain (disables SSO discovery).

x509_certificate.description: PEM-encoded X.509 signing certificate from the IdP.

UpdateServiceMonitorsRequest.description:
Replaces the service's HTTP and heartbeat links only. Deprecated: link and unlink one monitor
at a time with `POST /service/{id}/monitors` and `DELETE /service/{id}/monitors/{type}/{id}`.

description.description:
For the three fields below, `null` clears the value and leaving the
field out keeps it.

oneOf.description: `null` clears it; each field is optional and blank fields are dropped.

tags.description: Replaces the tags; `[]` clears them.

on_call_schedule_id.description: `null` clears it, so the policy's first level is on call.

UpdateShareRequest.description: Absent fields are kept; `expires_at: null` removes the expiry.

sla_target_percentage.description: SLA target percentage (e.g. 99.9). Send null to clear.

UpdateStatusPageBrandingRequest.description:
A field left out keeps its value and `null` clears it: `default_theme` goes
back to `system`, `white_label` to false, and every other field to unset.
An empty or blank text field clears it too.

logo_s3_key.description: The `s3_key` an upload of type `logo` returned.

logo_dark_s3_key.description:
The `s3_key` an upload of type `logo_dark` returned: the logo the page
shows in its dark theme. Without it the page shows the logo in both.

primary_color.description: `#rrggbb`. Colours the page title (without a logo) and headings.

accent_color.description:
`#rrggbb`. Colours the subscribe button, links, focus ring and chart
line; falls back to `primary_color`. The page adjusts both colours per
theme where needed to keep text and controls readable.

white_label.description: Hides the "Powered by Site Qwality" badge. `true` needs the White-Label pack.

oneOf.description: Leave out to keep the stored status, or to let a moved window decide it.

affected_http_job_ids.description: The monitors under maintenance. Required unless `whole_page` is true.

role.description:
One of `admin`, `member`, `viewer`. `owner` is not assignable here:
ownership transfer is a separate operation.
